question: Does the SPECIALS-versus-Watchtowers trade itself flip sign between maze A and maze B — i.e. is the roster-wide maze split found in the 2026-08-16 R2 fusion re-take a property of the spendDown control rather than of any fusion?
sigmaSource: hallHpAuc paired delta sd measured in the R2 regime by the registered regime-r2-adoption family (24,000 runs, n=3000/cell, 18/18 gates PASS): ~0.87 (maze A) / ~1.41 (maze B) across the three Watchtower ladder rungs. Maze B is the binding constraint. Identical to the sigma used by steam-vent-retune and by all five fusion-r2-* families, which is what makes this family's deltas directly comparable with theirs.

regime.label: R2
regime.justification: R2 with spendDown is the regime every fusion-r2-* family was taken in, and this family exists only to interrogate those families' shared baseline. Using any other regime would answer a different question. NO ARM FUSES: fuse:false everywhere, so the only thing varying is how many elemental specials the human holds and which partner element they are. The control holds NO special at all (freeSpecial:false), so under spendDown its entire budget converts to Watchtowers — making each non-control arm's delta exactly 'this special (or pair of specials) versus the Watchtowers the same gold would otherwise have bought'. The three partner arms reproduce, cell for cell, the CONTROL arms of fusion-r2-magma-trap (FIRE), fusion-r2-muddy-bog (WATER) and fusion-r2-grinder (WIND). humanElement is pinned to EARTH because those three fusions share it and yet split across mazes in opposite directions — if the split is carried by the control rather than the fusion, EARTH is where it must show.
regime.scopeLimit: FOUR limits. (1) R2 bars every TERMINAL measure: only 0-7% of runs end with the hall alive, so hallHpFrac and win rate are floor-censored; hallHpAuc is exempt as an integral over waves played, and wavesCleared is secondary despite being nearer a terminal measure. (2) ONE humanElement. A null here constrains the EARTH line only — it cannot clear FIRE (Firestorm) or WATER (Blizzard) of a genuinely per-fusion split, because their human class differs and that is the exact confound the three-family roster split exists to avoid. (3) The CROSS-POLICY GATE IS EMPTY — only scripted-v1 exists, and a stationary policy sites structures identically on both mazes. If the split IS a policy artifact this family will reproduce it faithfully and be unable to name it as one; only a second policy or a human playtest can separate those. This is the single most important limit here and it is declared up front. (4) TWO MAZES is the entire population. With n=2 any non-uniform effect can only present as a sign flip, so this family can establish that the trade flips, never that 'flipping' is abnormal.

positiveControl.expectedDirection: wt-x2 doubles Watchtower damage (3 -> 6) against a control that is ALL Watchtowers, and must land resolvably ABOVE control on hallHpAuc on BOTH mazes. regime-r2-adoption measured this rung at +0.713 (A) / +0.796 (B) with a free special present; this family removes the free special, so the magnitude is expected to be at least that large rather than equal to it, and only the SIGN and the both-mazes resolvability are committed. If this arm fails to separate, the instrument is not live in this family and nothing else in it may be read.

decisionRule:
Paired deltas against the pure-Watchtower control on hallHpAuc, per maze, for each of the four specials arms (earth-only, earth-fire, earth-water, earth-wind).

THE FAMILY ANSWERS A CONCORDANCE QUESTION, NOT A PASS/FAIL ONE. It is deliberately NOT written as 'does arm X clear a floor', because the 'passes on either maze' rule inherited from 2026-08-04 is what allowed the fusion roster to certify five arms that are each resolvably harmful on one maze. No arm here passes or fails anything.

SPLIT IS A CONTROL PROPERTY (the artifact hypothesis is SUPPORTED): for at least two of the four specials arms, delta_A and delta_B have OPPOSITE signs AND both cells are resolvable at BH-adjusted q < 0.05 across the declared family of 30 with the exact sign test agreeing in direction and the verdict surviving hang-imputation. Consequence if this fires: the five fusion-r2-* results are measuring their own baselines' maze preference, no fusion retune is warranted on that evidence, and the roster question must be re-asked against a control that does not itself flip.

SPLIT IS NOT A CONTROL PROPERTY (the artifact hypothesis is REFUTED): every specials arm whose two cells are both resolvable carries the SAME sign on both mazes. Consequence: the fusion-level split is a property of the fusions, and the next question is a design one (is a maze-situational fusion acceptable?) rather than an instrument one.

MIXED / UNRESOLVED: exactly one arm flips resolvably, or the arms disagree with each other, or fewer than two arms resolve on both mazes. Reported as unresolved. NO balance change and NO retraction of the fusion-r2-* corpus follows from an unresolved outcome — those numbers stand as taken either way; what is at stake here is only their INTERPRETATION.

ADDITIONAL DESCRIPTIVE READ, declared in advance and NOT a gate: whether each partner arm's maze preference matches the corresponding fusion's. fusion-r2 found Magma Trap (FIRE partner) +A/-B, Muddy Bog (WATER partner) +A/-B, Grinder (WIND partner) -A/+B. If earth-fire and earth-water prefer one maze and earth-wind the other, the control's preference tracks the fusion's and the artifact reading is strengthened. Recorded as a pattern to be tested by a later family, never as a verdict here.

SPLIT-HALF IS NOT A GATE and is reported for the record only, consistent with steam-vent-retune and the fusion-r2-* families.

MONOTONICITY: earth-only vs the three two-special arms form no ordered ladder (different partner elements are not doses), so no ordering argument may disqualify any arm.

CROSS-POLICY GATE NOT MET: only scripted-v1 exists. Every reading here is PROVISIONAL on it, and per scopeLimit (3) that provisionality is unusually load-bearing for this specific question.
whatWouldRefute:
PRE-REGISTERED PREDICTION, committed before the run. I expect the artifact hypothesis to be SUPPORTED — that at least two specials arms flip sign resolvably between mazes — because all five fusions in the 2026-08-16 re-take landed in the two discordant sign cells and none in the two concordant ones (probability ~3% if each fusion's two signs were independent coin flips), and a single shared cause is a better explanation of that than five independent tuning accidents.

The family REFUTES that prediction if every resolvable specials arm carries the same sign on both mazes. That outcome would mean the specials-versus-Watchtowers trade is maze-stable and the fusions genuinely are not, which puts the split back on the fusions and makes this family's premise wrong.

The family is UNINTERPRETABLE if wt-x2 fails to separate from control on both mazes: the instrument would not be live and no other cell may be read. It is also uninterpretable if fewer than two specials arms resolve on both mazes, and the response is to raise n rather than to declare the trade maze-stable.

A result where the control BEATS every specials arm on both mazes would say something larger than this family asks: that a single elemental special is simply worse than the Watchtowers its gold buys, which is a spec-level problem for the whole special/fusion system and not a maze-split question at all.
notes:
WHY THIS FAMILY EXISTS. The 2026-08-16 R2 fusion re-take (docs/reviews/2026-08-16-fusion-roster-r2-result.md) found all five remaining fusions technically passing the 'either maze' rule while EVERY one was resolvably harmful on its other maze. Two of the three EARTH fusions prefer maze A and the third prefers maze B, which rules out humanElement as the cause. The remaining candidate causes are (a) the spendDown Watchtower control has its own maze preference that the fusion delta inherits, (b) the stationary scripted policy sites structures identically on both mazes and manufactures the flip, or (c) five independent per-fusion accidents. THIS FAMILY SEPARATES (a) FROM (c) AND CANNOT TOUCH (b) — see scopeLimit (3).

familySize is 30 = 5 non-control arms x 2 mazes x 3 metrics, the family's own true width. It is NOT padded to the roster's 36: this family is not part of the roster question and inheriting the roster's padding would over-correct it.

SAMPLE SIZE. 1500 seeds x 2 postGaps = 3000 cells per arm per maze, against nRequired 2990 for MDE 0.10 on maze B. 6 arms x 2 mazes x 3000 = 36,000 runs, roughly 12 minutes.

SEEDS. 20330801+, a fresh disjoint set. Consumed so far: 20260801+ (fusion roster v1, mechanism family, wave-10 probe), 20270801+ (steam-vent replication), 20280801+ (R2 adoption), 20290801+ (steam-vent retune), 20300801+ (scald dial), 20310801+ (slow dial), 20320801+ (the R2 fusion roster re-take).

No balance change ships from this family under any outcome. It decides how the existing fusion corpus should be READ, which is a prerequisite to deciding whether any retune is warranted at all.
